reasons: correct: The full-rectangle replacement for an empty raw Hall region is an off-coverage totalization with nonzero length. At boundary parameters such as \(\alpha_{xa}=4\), the two threshold count errors have a nondegenerate limiting distribution, so the fixed-level Clopper--Pearson strips can imply only indices above four with a positive limiting probability; the raw region is then empty. On that event the full rectangle makes the maximal width order \(\ell\), defeating the asserted \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) width even though coverage may fail there. Replacing an empty raw region and an empty final intersection by singletons changes output only off the joint count-coverage event, preserves the exact coverage proof, and gives zero rather than global fallback length.
Keep the interval symbol total and length-controlled when its bias-expanded core interval misses the global Hall interval off the simultaneous coverage event.
Synchronize the symbol catalog with the corrected empty-region totalization; the former full rectangle can force a nonshrinking width on a fixed positive-probability off-coverage event.
